_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 9. Blau notes: 9:5 (Saadia's tripartite 'prohibition/restraint/command'; Blau prefers 'prohibition' over Kapach's 'warning'), 9:6 (Cairo includes 'כל'; Blau notes Petersburg lacks it). Saadia-specific moves: 9:3 inserts 'טאהר' (pure) into 'every creeping thing'; 9:16 inserts 'לאמאן אלדהר מן אללה' = 'as eternal security from God' (interpretive addition); 9:22 'באלסוק' = 'in the marketplace' (concretizes Hebrew בחוץ); 9:25 'מלעון אבא כנעאן' = 'cursed is the father of Canaan' (Saadia interpretively redirects the curse from Canaan the grandson to Ham the offender); 9:27 'יחסן אללה ליפת' = 'may God grant good to Japheth' (interprets יפת as related to good/benefit).

translations.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons; and He said to them: 'Bear fruit and multiply, and fill the earth.
translations.2: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon all the wild creatures of the earth, and upon the bird of the sky, and upon everything that creeps upon the earth, and upon the fish of the sea — they are delivered into your hands.
translations.3: And every pure living creeping thing shall be for you as food, just as the green herbage — I have given you everything.
translations.4: But the flesh — do not eat it with its blood, for that is its soul.
translations.5: But as for your own blood, from yourselves I shall require it by prohibition; and from the hand of the wild beast I shall require it by restraint; and from the hand of the rest of the people I shall require it by command. Any human who has killed his brother — I shall require his soul of him.
translations.6: Such that whoever sheds the blood of a human — by another human shall his blood be shed; for in the form of God, sovereign, He made him.
translations.7: And you — bear fruit and multiply; move forth in the earth and multiply upon it.'
translations.8: Then God said to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying:
translations.9: 'Behold, I establish My covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
translations.10: and with every living soul that is with you — from the bird to the beast, and all the wild creatures of the earth that are with you, of all that went out of the ark — for all the wild creatures of the earth.
translations.11: And I establish My covenant with you: no corporeal being shall ever again be cut off by the water of the flood; and never shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.'
translations.12: And God said: 'This is the sign of the covenant which I am setting between Me and you, and between every living soul that is with you, for the generations of eternity:
translations.13: My bow — I have set it in the cloud; and it shall become a sign of covenant between Me and the dwellers of the earth.
translations.14: And when I cause cloud to gather over the earth, the bow shall appear in the cloud;
translations.15: and I shall remember My covenant which is between Me and you, and between every living soul of every corporeal being; and the water shall not again become a flood to destroy every corporeal being.
translations.16: And the bow shall be in the cloud — I shall cause it to appear — as a remembrance of eternal security from God for every living soul, in every corporeal being which is upon the face of the earth.'
translations.17: And God said to Noah: 'This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between Me and every corporeal being that is upon the earth.'
translations.18: And the sons of Noah who went out from the ark were Shem and Ham and Japheth; and Ham was called the father of Canaan.
translations.19: These three were the sons of Noah; and from them was all the earth dispersed.
translations.20: And when Noah began with the tilling of the earth, he planted a vineyard.
translations.21: And he drank of the wine and became drunk; and he was uncovered within his tent.
translations.22: And Ham the father of Canaan saw his father's nakedness, and told his two brothers in the marketplace.
translations.23: And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and placed it upon both their shoulders; and they walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness, with their faces turned backward; and their father's nakedness they did not see.
translations.24: And when Noah awoke from his drunkenness, he knew what his youngest son had done to him.
translations.25: And he said: 'Cursed is the father of Canaan; a slave of slaves shall he be to his brothers.'
translations.26: Then he said: 'Blessed be God the God of Shem; and may the father of Canaan be a slave to him.
translations.27: May God grant good to Japheth; and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and may the father of Canaan be a slave to them.'
translations.28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
translations.29: And the whole of his lifetime came to nine hundred and fifty years; and then he died.
